issues.evidence: ས་འདི་ཀུན་ཏུ་འཁྲུགས: ཀུན་ཏུ is "everywhere/throughout" (Kunpal 8-68: ཀུན་ཏུ་ཁྱབ་ཅིང་འཁྲུགས་པ, "pervading and agitating"), not an intensifier of the degree of agitation.

issues.span: If not, my suffering too is like that of sentient beings.
issues.evidence: དེ་མིན་བདག་ཀྱང་སེམས་ཅན་བཞིན: the elided verb is བཟློག "averted": if it is not to be averted, then I too, like (other) sentient beings, am not to be averted/protected. Sanskrit na ced ātmāpi sattvavat; bo-kunpal 8-102: བདག་གི་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཀྱང་སེམས་ཅན་གཞན་གྱི་བཞིན་དུ་བཟློག་བྱ་མིན་པར་མཚུངས; bo-shenga 8-102: བཟློག་པར་མི་བྱའོ. The English "is like that of sentient beings" omits the conclusion that my own suffering would then also not be averted.
issues.fix: If it is not (to be averted), then my own suffering too, like that of other sentient beings, is not to be averted.

issues.evidence: The Tibetan is a four-line verse (བདག་མེད་ལུས་འདི་ལ། / གོམས་པས་བདག་གི་བློ་བྱུང་བ། / དེ་བཞིན་སེམས་ཅན་གཞན་ལ་ཡང་། / གོམས་པས་བདག་བློ་ཅིས་མི་སྐྱེ།), but the English is one line with capitals after commas, so the line breaks are lost.
issues.fix:
Just as towards this selfless body,
The intellect of self has arisen through habituation,
Likewise towards other sentient beings as well,
Why should the intellect of self not arise through habituation?

issues.evidence: བདག་མེད་ལུས་འདི་ལ: བདག་མེད་ here qualifies the body (Sanskrit nirātmake; bo-kunpal 8-114: བདག་མེད་པའི་ཕ་མའི་ཁུ་ཁྲག་ཡོངས་སུ་སྨིན་པའི་ལུས་འདི, a body without a self), so "body of selflessness" misleadingly makes selflessness a property or substance of the body.

issues.span: even wandering beings' fear in assemblies
issues.evidence: འཁོར་གྱི་འཇིགས་པའང་བསལ་བའི་ཕྱིར: the emphasis (ཡང/ང) falls on the fear, even the slight timidity in assemblies (Sanskrit pariṣaccharadyabhayam api; bo-shenga/bo-gyaltsab 8-117: འཁོར་གྱི་ནང་དུ་བག་ཚ་བའི་འཇིགས་པའང་). The English placement of 'even' before 'wandering beings' suggests the beings are what is emphasised.
issues.fix: to dispel even the fear (timidity) of wandering beings in assemblies

issues.span:
This one is great in the world, and
I am known as inferior
issues.evidence: གྲག/གྲགས "is known/reputed" governs both clauses (Sanskrit kila after both mahān and nīcaḥ; bo-shenga 8-141: འཇིག་རྟེན་ལ་ཆེ་བར་གྲགས་པ; bo-kunpal: ཆེ་བའི་ཡོན་ཏན་དང་ལྡན་པར་གྲགས་པ). The English asserts "great" outright and puts "known" only on the speaker.
issues.fix:
This one is renowned as great in the world, and
I am known as inferior and without good qualities.

issues.span:
what is not the perfect happiness of a Buddha—
such a situation as this could not possibly occur
issues.evidence: སངས་རྒྱས་ཕུན་སུམ་བདེ་མིན་པ། གནས་སྐབས་འདི་འདྲར་འགྱུར་མི་སྲིད: the situation (གནས་སྐབས) is one that is NOT the perfect happiness of a Buddha, i.e. suffering (bo-gyaltsab 8-156: སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་དོན་གཉིས་ཕུན་སུམ་ཚོགས་པའི་བདེ་བ་མིན་པ་སྡུག་བསྔལ་མྱོང་བའི་གནས་སྐབས་འདི་འདྲར་འགྱུར་མི་སྲིད; bo-shenga 8-156). The English fragment "what is not..." followed by a dash does not make clear that it qualifies "such a situation".
issues.fix: a situation such as this, which is not the perfect happiness of a Buddha, could not possibly occur.
